description: A four-panel composite figure of 3D ball-and-stick crystal-structure models (Materials Project / DFT derived) for the Fe–20Mn–9Al–1.5C lightweight austenitic steel family. A single shared legend below the panels identifies the spheres: gold = Fe/Mn, cream/white = Ni, blue = Al, dark grey = C. (a) "disordered γ" shows an FCC unit cell in which blue (Al) and gold (Fe/Mn) spheres are randomly intermixed over the vertex and face-centre positions. (b) "ordered γ" shows the same FCC cell in an ordered arrangement, with one species on the vertices and the others on the face centres (caption: Al at the vertex, Fe and Mn at face centres). (c) "κ-carbide" shows a perovskite/E21-type cell with Al corners, Fe/Mn faces and a dark-grey C sphere on the body-centred (1/2,1/2,1/2) octahedral interstitial. (d) "AlNi3C" shows a Ni-rich κ-carbide variant in which cream Ni spheres enter the cell alongside Al and C. No axes, scale bars, crystallographic indices or numeric values are printed on any panel; all four models are drawn at the same schematic scale. The figure establishes the structural distinction between disordered/ordered austenite and the κ-carbide arrangement that underpins the formation-energy discussion.

observations.observation: The shared legend identifies the four sphere colours exactly as: gold = Fe/Mn, cream/white = Ni, blue = Al, dark grey = C.
Panel (a) is labelled 'disordered γ' and shows blue Al and gold Fe/Mn spheres randomly intermixed on FCC vertex and face-centre positions, with no ordering.
Panel (b) is labelled 'ordered γ' and shows the same FCC-type cell with the Al and Fe/Mn spheres segregated onto distinct sublattices.
Panel (c) is labelled 'κ-carbide' and contains a single dark-grey C sphere at the body centre of a perovskite-type cell, in contrast to the C-free cells in (a) and (b).
Panel (d) is labelled 'AlNi3C' and is the only panel containing cream/white Ni spheres, marking it as the Ni-rich κ-carbide variant.
None of the four panels carries axes, crystallographic indices, scale bars or printed numeric values; all are schematic 3D unit-cell models drawn at the same scale.
The caption states the four structures are (a) disordered γ, (b) ordered γ, (c) κ-carbide, and (d) AlNi3C (described as one of the Ni-rich κ-carbides).

The citing text states that in Fe–20Mn–9Al–1.5C-xNi-yCr steels the Fe, Mn and Al atoms randomly occupy the vertex and face-centre positions of the FCC lattice, producing the disordered γ of panel (a).
The citing text states that when Al occupies the vertex and Fe and Mn the face centres, the ordered γ-austenite phase of panel (b) forms.

The citing text states that κ-carbides form when C progressively occupies the body-centred (1/2,1/2,1/2) octahedral interstitials, are perovskite/E21 structures, and have ideal stoichiometry (Fe, Mn)AlC.
The citing text states the structures and energies were obtained by first-principles calculations from the Materials Project database using DFT-GGA with the PBE functional.

subfigures.description: 3D ball-and-stick model labelled 'disordered γ': an FCC-like cell in which blue (Al) and gold (Fe/Mn) spheres are randomly distributed over both vertex and face-centre sites, with no long-range order.
3D ball-and-stick model labelled 'ordered γ': the same FCC-type cell but with the spheres in an ordered sublattice arrangement (caption states Al at the vertices, Fe and Mn at the face centres).

3D ball-and-stick model labelled 'κ-carbide': a perovskite-type cell with gold Fe/Mn and blue Al spheres on the lattice sites and a single dark-grey C sphere occupying the body centre, i.e. the (1/2,1/2,1/2) octahedral interstitial.

3D ball-and-stick model labelled 'AlNi3C': a Ni-rich κ-carbide cell containing cream/white Ni spheres together with blue Al and dark-grey C spheres, illustrating one of the Ni-rich κ-carbide variants.
